Hybrid text rendering: small recognized labels become readable terminal text,
and large recognized letters become ASCII contours at their original size.
The mode is enabled by default; use `--text off` for the v0.1 renderer.

Windows Terminal:

```powershell
.\nesterm.exe ".\Super Mario Bros. 3 (Europe).nes" --size 64x30
```

Linux/macOS:

```sh
./nesterm /path/to/game.nes --size 64x30
```

No Rust, Cargo, Node.js, or OCR service is required. Bring your own ROM.

## Changes

- Readable small text with exact bitmap matching and a verified European Mario 3
  font profile: player menu, `Nintendo`, copyright, `WORLD`, scores and timers.
- Large recognized `SUPER`, `MARIO BROS.` and `3` are drawn with ASCII contours.
  The actual font graphics are read from the user's ROM; no game assets are shipped.
- Optional `--text-font path.json` maps a game's bitmap glyphs to single-column
  Unicode, including Cyrillic. Archives include the `Привет` format example and
  `docs/text-rendering.md`.
- UTF-8 full/diff output and asciicast recording preserve literal Unicode cells.
- Unknown and partly hidden alphabetic words remain graphics. No dictionary
  completion or automatic translation is performed.

Font matching is not universal OCR. Ordered Latin/digit sets in other CHR-ROMs
can be discovered heuristically, but stylized fonts, CHR-RAM fonts and ROM hacks
may need a custom map. The built-in game profile requires the verified CHR layout.
Contour detail depends on terminal resolution; `64x30` is recommended.

## Validation and packaging

Synthetic tests cover both grids, Cyrillic, scaled contours, noise, unknown
letters, font validation, Unicode replacements and byte-exact recording. The
user-supplied Mario 3 ROM was also checked locally without committing its data.
The original renderer continues to match all 72 upstream reference frames.
Native release builds test Linux, Windows and both macOS architectures; real
PTY scenarios run on Linux and macOS. Rust 1.88 is the minimum supported version.

[SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/vertigo-red/nesterm-rust/releases/download/v0.2.0/SHA256SUMS)
contains checksums for all four archives. Linux is static musl, Windows includes
the static C runtime, and macOS targets version 13 or newer. macOS binaries are
not Apple-signed or notarized. Every archive includes application, font,
dependency and standard-library notices. Audio and save-file persistence remain
outside the application scope.
